description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by country or region of origin, as presented in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning 2012 to 2022. Each year displays a grouped set of vertical bars, color-coded according to the legend: blue for “Other,” orange for “USA,” green for “IN” (India), red for “UK,” purple for “IT” (Italy), and brown for “DE” (Germany). In 2012 and 2013, only the USA contributed datasets (1 each). In 2014, “Other” and USA each contributed 1 dataset. In 2015, “Other” contributed 1 and “DE” contributed 1. In 2016, “Other” (2), “USA” (5), “IN” (3), and “UK” (2) contributed datasets. In 2017, “Other” (15), “USA” (12), “UK” (8), and “IT” (5) contributed. In 2018, “Other” (15), “USA” (10), “IN” (3), “UK” (3), “IT” (3), and “DE” (3) contributed. In 2019, “Other” (30), “USA” (15), “IN” (5), “UK” (2), and “IT” (7) contributed. In 2020, “Other” (60), “USA” (25), “IN” (10), “UK” (12), “IT” (2), and “DE” (15) contributed. In 2021, “Other” (100), “USA” (30), “IN” (20), “UK” (15), “IT” (10), and “DE” (8) contributed. In 2022, “Other” (30), “USA” (4), “IN” (8), and “UK” (7) contributed, with “IT” contributing 1. The “Other” category consistently dominates in dataset volume, especially peaking in 2021 at 100 datasets, while contributions from individual countries vary significantly across years. The chart visually emphasizes the growing volume of datasets over time, particularly from 2017 onward, and highlights the dominance of non-country-specific or multi-country datasets under “Other.”
